Rate a card

Choose a score from 1 to 10.

Tap or drag the Affinity bar. Your choice is saved immediately, then the next card appears.

Why ratings matter

Ratings help improve later suggestions.

Your score shows how interested you are in the person or pair on the card. MyScoutee can use it with other signals to make future suggestions more relevant.

Photos and profile

See more before you rate.

Tap the left or right side of the image to browse photos. Use the eye icon to open the full profile.

Filters and modes

Choose which cards you want to see.

The filter button narrows the results, and its number shows how many matches remain. Use Preferences, Friends in Common, Inside Network, or Outside Network to switch card groups.

Rating history

Review or change an earlier rating.

Open history from the header. To change a rating later, open Activity ratings and select its star action.

Got it
Choose an event list

Open the group you need.

Switch between all or active events, pending items, invitations, your events, drafts, and trash. Use Explore for public events or the plus button to create one.

Read an event card

See the key details at a glance.

The card shows the event image, title, time, place, and organizer. A badge such as 1 / 5 shows accepted people against capacity, while a red number marks pending items.

People and actions

Open members or the actions available to you.

Tap the capacity badge to see participants and pending people. The three-dot menu changes with your role and the event state, so it may offer viewing, editing, publishing, invitation handling, sharing, leaving, deleting, or restoring.

Join an event

The steps depend on the event settings.

You can accept or reject an invitation from its card. Some events confirm you immediately; others require approval, a ticket, accepted rules, payment, or choices before your place is final.

Create or host

Start simple and add details when needed.

The plus button opens the event editor. You can create a basic meetup or add sub-events, groups, resources, tickets, pricing, and capacity rules.
